title: What the close tells us
text: Tech had a rough Monday. The Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ fell 1.4% to $681.09 and the S&P 500 fund SPY fell 0.5% to $752.15. Inside the Nasdaq, tech companies fell about 3.5% on average, while makers of everyday products rose about 2.4%. Tomorrow, watch AMD, which reports its results after the market closes. A calm reaction does not mean the worry is gone, and a big drop does not mean a crash. This is for learning, not advice.

title: AMD leads the chip drop
text: AMD fell 7.5% to $466.84, the biggest drop on our list. Vertiv fell 3.5% to $224.39 and Rocket Lab fell 4.9% to $52.07. Microsoft fell 2.8% to $507.12. These companies are tied to AI and fast growth, so they tend to swing together.

title: AMD reports results tomorrow
text: AMD will share its third quarter results on Tuesday after the market closes. Analysts expect about $13.1 billion in sales. When a company reports, the price can jump or drop based on how the numbers compare with what people hoped for, not only on the numbers themselves.

title: GE and Amazon rise on a down day
text: GE Aerospace rose 4.6% to $315.81 and Amazon rose 2.2% to $245.63, while Lockheed Martin edged up 1.0% to $643.22. Our data does not say why they rose. It shows that on the same day, different industries can move in opposite directions.

title: Lesson 33: What is concentration risk?
text: Concentration risk means having too much of your money tied to one company, one industry or one idea. If that one thing has a bad day, your whole pile feels it. Today is a good example. Chip makers like AMD, Vertiv and TSMC often move together, so owning only chip stocks can feel like owning one big bet. Spreading money across different kinds of companies, such as health care, defense or broad index funds, can soften a rough day in one area. It does not remove risk, and it does not guarantee gains. It just helps one surprise matter less.
